input.quote: NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, RELIANCE OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES OR LOST OR IMPUTED PROFITS OR ROYALTIES OR COST OF PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES
input.rationale: Section 15.11 (p0833) is the only limitation-of-liability provision: it contains a mutual indirect/consequential damages waiver (already meeting that element) but no aggregate monetary cap. Article 12 (indemnification), the 13.6 disclaimer and 14.4.2 (which only channels SFJ's termination damages into the Section 14.2 payments) add no cap, and document-wide searches for \"aggregate liability\"/\"shall not exceed\" return nothing responsive, so both Parties' direct liability is unlimited and the rule fails. We cure at the preferred level: because Article 6 payments are event/approval-driven and a bare twelve-month lookback could compute to nil, the greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor is needed to make the mutual cap real, which also completes the preferred formula together with the data protection/security, fraud and IP-infringement carve-outs. The basis is anchored to PB's Article 6 payments because this Co-Development Agreement has no \"fees\" concept, and the retained savings sentence is extended in place so all PB payment obligations are not \"damages\" subject to the cap. Nothing else in 15.11 is disturbed; the SFJ Article 4 funding carve-out proposed earlier has been dropped as outside the checklist.

proposal.summary: Add mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' Article 6 payments and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped carve-outs for indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirm PB's payment obligations are not capped damages
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 15.11 waives indirect damages but leaves both Parties' direct liability entirely uncapped, so we have added a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' Article 6 payments (this Agreement has no defined "fees") and USD 1,000,000, the floor being necessary because Article 6 payments are event-driven and could otherwise be nil. Indemnification, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and PB's payment obligations are not "damages" subject to it.

ops.text: Except for each Party's indemnification obligations under Article 12, each Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article 10, each Party's breach of its data protection or security obligations, each Party's gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud, and each Party's infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed the greater of (a) the amounts paid or payable by PB to SFJ under Article 6 in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) One Million U.S. Dollars ($1,000,000).

ops.oldText: FOR THE AVOIDANCE OF DOUBT, THIS SECTION 15.11 IS NOT MEANT TO LIMIT PB'S OBLIGATION TO PAY SFJ THE AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 6 OR SECTION 14.2.
ops.newText: FOR THE AVOIDANCE OF DOUBT, THIS SECTION 15.11 IS NOT MEANT TO LIMIT PB'S OBLIGATION TO PAY SFJ THE AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 6 OR SECTION 14.2, OR ANY OTHER PB PAYMENT OBLIGATION, WHICH ARE NOT "DAMAGES" SUBJECT TO ANY CAP.
